1→---
name: to-spec
description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

This skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user — just synthesize what you already know.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.
10→
## Process

1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.

2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.

Check with the user that these seams match their expectations.

3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.
20→
<spec-template>

## Problem Statement

The problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.

## Solution

The solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.
30→
## User Stories

A LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:

1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>

<user-story-example>
1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending
</user-story-example>
40→
This list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.

## Implementation Decisions

A list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:

- The modules that will be built/modified
- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified
- Technical clarifications from the developer
50→- Architectural decisions
- Schema changes
- API contracts
- Specific interactions

Do NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.

Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

## Testing Decisions
60→
A list of testing decisions that were made. Include:

- A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)
- Which modules will be tested
- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)

## Out of Scope

A description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.
70→
## Further Notes

Any further notes about the feature.

</spec-template>

1→---
name: to-tickets
description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.
10→
The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)
20→
If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>
30→
- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

40→**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

50→Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

60→Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

<local-ticket-template>
70→
# <NN> — <Ticket title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1
80→- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

</local-ticket-template>

<issue-template>

## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

90→## What to build

The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Blocked by
100→
- A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

</issue-template>

In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# To Tickets

Break a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets** — tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

### 1. Gather context

Work from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker

Publish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured — the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:

- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's "Blocked by" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below — one ticket per file, never a single combined file.
- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's "Blocked by" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise — the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.

Do NOT close or modify any parent issue.

<local-ticket-template>

# <NN> — <Ticket title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or "None — can start immediately".

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2

</local-ticket-template>

<issue-template>

## Parent

A reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).

## What to build

The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective — not layer-by-layer implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Blocked by

- A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

</issue-template>

In either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets — they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

1→---
name: grilling
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
---

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled — the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

10→Each question should be formatted like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree — settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

20→Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it — don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report — ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's — put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

1→---
name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
---

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline — challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill — that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

10→## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
20→│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/
30→│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── CONTEXT.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

40→Create files lazily — only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y — which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

50→When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account' — do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible — which is right?"

60→### Update CONTEXT.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up — capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).

`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

70→1. **Hard to reverse** — the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context** — a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off** — there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

## Pause, resume, list, open

```bash
dora harness list
dora harness pause <slug>
dora harness resume <slug>
dora harness open <slug>
```
100→
`pause` skips later runs of that routine only. Other routines keep going. A run that already started may finish. `resume` starts later runs again. `list` shows each slug as running, paused, or none. `open` opens the routine folder.

Close the laptop and the Mac sleeps. Jobs do not run while the Mac sleeps. That is not pause. Due jobs can fire on wake if the job is not paused.

## Defaults

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| How often it runs | every 1 hour |
110→| One-pass time limit | 10 minutes |
| Night stop if the job sits idle | 10 minutes (Hermes default) |

You can change the interval and the one-pass limit per routine. A busy night job can keep going past 10 minutes if it is still working.

## Common mistakes

- Treating laptop close as `dora harness pause`. Sleep stops the clock. It does not pause the job.
- Expecting Dora to finish `hermes mcp login scalekit`. You run that in a real terminal.
- Re-running `--accept` on the same slug. Dora refuses to overwrite the folder.
120→- Expecting a Dora logs verb. Use the Runtime watch commands Dora prints.
- Using Hermes `--script` as the freeze path. A Skill script is local work inside the Skill.
- Putting a `scripts/` folder next to `prompt.md`.
- Expecting a chat app in the harness. Connectors live on a use case, not in this group.

## Related

- [Run a pocket agent](/get-started/pocket-agents/)
- [Commands](/commands/)
- [Skills](/get-started/skills/)

1→# 55 Hermes cron tick-state (notepad, continuity, monitor, workdir, MEMORY.md)

_Research · 2026-09-02 · Local Hermes source + `--help` + official docs. Research only. Does not change product code._

**Question:** Hermes cron has tick-state tools (notepad, `--continuity`, `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url`, `--workdir`, MEMORY.md). Dora boots pocket agents onto Hermes. Can Dora input or leverage those capabilities in pocket-agent setup, and which ones should it?

**Pinned binary:** local Hermes Agent **v0.20.6** (2026.8.27), upstream `32fe1293`, local `44656326` (+1 carried commit), install `/Users/saif/.hermes/hermes-agent`, PATH `/Users/saif/.local/bin/hermes`. **732 commits behind** at capture. Official pages: [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [cron internals](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/cron-internals), [automate-with-cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/automate-with-cron), [memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts` (includes `8076419` footer), `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`, `src/core/routine.ts`, `skills/writing-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `skills/grilling-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `apps/website/content/get-started/pocket-agents.mdx`. Prior note: [`54-hermes-provider.md`](./54-hermes-provider.md).
10→
**Trust rule:** Dora must speak the installed binary. When live docs and local `--help` / source disagree, this note trusts the local tree.

---

## Mental model

Each Hermes cron tick is a **new agent session**. Tick-state is not conversation history. It is something Hermes **injects into this tick's prompt**, or a **file the agent can read**, or a **cheap pre-LLM hash skip**.

| Store | Who writes | Who reads next tick | What it actually is |
20→|-------|------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Fresh session (default) | Nobody | Nothing from last tick | New `AIAgent`. No prior transcript. |
| Notepad | Agent via `hermes cron notepad <job_id> set` (terminal CLI; no model tool) | Scheduler prepends KV if non-empty | Per-**hex job id** SQLite, 16 KB/key, 64 KB/job |
| `--continuity` | Hermes, after a run that produced output | Scheduler prepends last `*.md` output (8k cap) | Last **report text**, not a cursor |
| Monitor hash | Scheduler, from script/URL bytes | Unchanged → **no LLM**. Changed → diff block | Exact-byte SHA-256 skip |
| `--workdir` | Agent via file tools in that dir | Next tick, same dir | cwd + optional `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` |
| MEMORY.md / USER.md | Agent `memory` tool | Every session, including cron | Shared profile notes. Not per-job. Not a cursor. |

Dora already owns a folder: `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/` (`prompt.md`, `routine.yml`, copied skills, optional `.env`). Hermes job **name** is that slug. Hermes job **id** is a new 12-char hex on every `cron create`.

30→---

## 1. Default isolation: fresh session

Default cron is amnesia for the **conversation**. Official cron page: jobs "run in fresh agent sessions with the normal static tool list." Official internals: "Create fresh `AIAgent` session (no conversation history)." Local internals: no previous-run transcript; prompt must be self-contained; `cronjob` toolset disabled.

Local fire path still **does** load profile memory (`skip_memory=False`) and `SOUL.md`. It does **not** load project context files unless `--workdir` is set (`skip_context_files=not bool(_job_workdir)`).

So: not a blank model. It is a blank **thread**. Preferences in MEMORY.md can leak in. Last Slack ts cannot, unless one of the stores above is used.

40→Cron also disables `messaging` and `clarify` always, and `cronjob` unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling` is on. Terminal stays available. That is how notepad writes are supposed to happen.

_Research · 2026-09-02 · Local Hermes source + `--help` + official docs. Research only. Does not change product code._

**Question:** Hermes cron has tick-state tools (notepad, `--continuity`, `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url`, `--workdir`, MEMORY.md). Dora boots pocket agents onto Hermes. Can Dora input or leverage those capabilities in pocket-agent setup, and which ones should it?

**Pinned binary:** local Hermes Agent **v0.20.6** (2026.8.27), upstream `32fe1293`, local `44656326` (+1 carried commit), install `/Users/saif/.hermes/hermes-agent`, PATH `/Users/saif/.local/bin/hermes`. **732 commits behind** at capture. Official pages: [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [cron internals](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/cron-internals), [automate-with-cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/automate-with-cron), [memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts` (includes `8076419` footer), `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`, `src/core/routine.ts`, `skills/writing-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `skills/grilling-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `apps/website/content/get-started/pocket-agents.mdx`. Prior note: [`54-hermes-provider.md`](./54-hermes-provider.md).

**Trust rule:** Dora must speak the installed binary. When live docs and local `--help` / source disagree, this note trusts the local tree.

---

## Mental model

Each Hermes cron tick is a **new agent session**. Tick-state is not conversation history. It is something Hermes **injects into this tick's prompt**, or a **file the agent can read**, or a **cheap pre-LLM hash skip**.

| Store | Who writes | Who reads next tick | What it actually is |
|-------|------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Fresh session (default) | Nobody | Nothing from last tick | New `AIAgent`. No prior transcript. |
| Notepad | Agent via `hermes cron notepad <job_id> set` (terminal CLI; no model tool) | Scheduler prepends KV if non-empty | Per-**hex job id** SQLite, 16 KB/key, 64 KB/job |
| `--continuity` | Hermes, after a run that produced output | Scheduler prepends last `*.md` output (8k cap) | Last **report text**, not a cursor |
| Monitor hash | Scheduler, from script/URL bytes | Unchanged → **no LLM**. Changed → diff block | Exact-byte SHA-256 skip |
| `--workdir` | Agent via file tools in that dir | Next tick, same dir | cwd + optional `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` |
| MEMORY.md / USER.md | Agent `memory` tool | Every session, including cron | Shared profile notes. Not per-job. Not a cursor. |

Dora already owns a folder: `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/` (`prompt.md`, `routine.yml`, copied skills, optional `.env`). Hermes job **name** is that slug. Hermes job **id** is a new 12-char hex on every `cron create`.

---

## 1. Default isolation: fresh session

Default cron is amnesia for the **conversation**. Official cron page: jobs "run in fresh agent sessions with the normal static tool list." Official internals: "Create fresh `AIAgent` session (no conversation history)." Local internals: no previous-run transcript; prompt must be self-contained; `cronjob` toolset disabled.

Local fire path still **does** load profile memory (`skip_memory=False`) and `SOUL.md`. It does **not** load project context files unless `--workdir` is set (`skip_context_files=not bool(_job_workdir)`).

So: not a blank model. It is a blank **thread**. Preferences in MEMORY.md can leak in. Last Slack ts cannot, unless one of the stores above is used.

Cron also disables `messaging` and `clarify` always, and `cronjob` unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling` is on. Terminal stays available. That is how notepad writes are supposed to happen.

### Agent-browser per-command `--help`

100→`print_command_help(command)` returns a hand-written page. Typical shape (`open`, `click`, `doctor`):

1. One-line what it is
2. `Usage:` line
3. Short prose (why / gotchas)
4. Options, then Global Options (`--json`, `--session`)
5. Examples (copy-paste)
6. Sometimes Exit codes (`doctor` documents `0` / `1`)

### Doraval top-level `--help` (citty default)

Ran `bun run src/cli/index.ts --help` (32 lines). Banner from `src/cli/index.ts` `meta.description`:

```

120→Primary: scan · review · fix · new --for <agent>.
Tip: point a coding agent at this CLI, or run `dora` (scan). Docs: https://doraval.dev
```

Then citty `USAGE` + `OPTIONS` + flat `COMMANDS` (12 names). No groups in the printed list. `command-tree.ts` comments split “primary” vs “tooling”; citty does not show that.

**Voice:** Reader-ish (human tip + docs URL). Not the first loop in [`CONTEXT.md`](../../CONTEXT.md) (`npx skills add` then `dora review --quick`). `--help` never says `review --quick`.

**Missing vs AB:** examples, env vars, grouped catalog, “Start here” with a runnable command, exit-code table.

`dora scan --help` is 12 lines. `dora fix --help` has `--brief` / `--yes` / `--dry-run` but no example lines. `dora memory --help` lists subcommands only.

140→Runtime *does* teach next steps (`nextAction` in `out.ts`; scan “Next” suggestions; review → `dora fix`). That teaching is after a run, not in `--help`.

| | Agent-browser | Doraval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| From `--help` alone | Yes. “Start here” → `skills get core --full` → core loop in that skill (`open` → `snapshot -i` → `click @eN`). | Partial. Banner says run `dora` (scan). Does not name `dora review --quick`. |

150→
An agent that only has `dora --help` does **not** learn the CONTEXT.md first loop. An agent that only has `agent-browser --help` is told exactly one next command.

name: ask-dora
description: >-
  Use when the teammate types /ask-dora, or asks any Dora question, a
  routine idea, a pocket job, dora harness new, or a connector catalog
  question.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

10→# ask-dora

User-invoked router for an internal teammate. One name. Use a primitive. Do not hold that primitive's craft here.

## Empty

Print this map. Then stop.

```
Dora jobs: review, fix, unused, scan. Load review-with-dora.
20→Routine flow: a routine, a loop, recurring, a routine idea, a pocket job, or harness new.
  Load grilling-for-routine. Night prompt: writing-for-routine.
After a routine exists: dora harness boot, pause, resume, list, open.
If Hermes is missing: print official install steps. Dora does not install Hermes.
If a Scalekit AgentKit skill is missing: install scalekit-inc/authstack, then reload skills.
```

## Route

1. Read the ask.
30→2. If a routine already exists and the ask is boot, pause, resume, list, open, or watch: name that `dora harness` verb. Do not load the grill.
3. If it is a routine, a loop, recurring, a routine idea, a pocket job, or `dora harness new`: load `grilling-for-routine`. Done: that skill is loaded.
4. If it is a Dora job (review, fix, unused, scan): load `review-with-dora`. Done: that skill is loaded.
5. If the ask is only the public connector catalog (what exists, tool names):
   If `discover-connectors` is on disk: load it. Done.
   If missing: print official install. Stop.
6. If the ask is add or configure a Scalekit dashboard **connection**:
   If `setup-agentkit` is on disk: load it. Done.
   If missing: print official install. Stop.
7. If the ask is a **connected account**, OAuth link, or calling Slack/GitHub as that account:
40→   If `integrate-agentkit` is on disk: load it. Done.
   If missing: print official install. Stop.
8. Else: name the matching `dora` verb from `dora --help --json`. Done: the teammate has the next command.

Look up facts (skill on disk, Hermes present, AgentKit skills present). Leave slug, connector, and interval to the human.
If Hermes is missing and the ask needs a Tick or boot: print official install steps. Do not fake a pass.

When the needed AgentKit skill is missing:
50→
```
Install Scalekit authstack. Follow:
https://docs.scalekit.com/dev-kit/build-with-ai/
npx skills add scalekit-inc/authstack
Then reload skills or restart the session and try again.
```

MUST load `grilling-for-routine` for a routine, a loop, recurring, a routine idea, a pocket job, or harness new.

MUST NOT invent a connector catalog or dashboard steps.

1→---
name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

# Setup Matt Pocock's Skills

Scaffold the per-repo configuration that the engineering skills assume:
10→
- **Issue tracker** — where issues live (GitHub by default; local markdown is also supported out of the box)
- **Triage labels** — the strings used for the five canonical triage roles
- **Domain docs** — where `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs live, and the consumer rules for reading them

This is a prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script. Explore, present what you found, confirm with the user, then write.

## Process

### 1. Explore
20→
Look at the current repo to understand its starting state. Read whatever exists; don't assume:

- `git remote -v` and `.git/config` — is this a GitHub repo? Which one?
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root — does either exist? Is there already an `## Agent skills` section in either?
- `CONTEXT.md` and `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root
- `docs/adr/` and any `src/*/docs/adr/` directories
- `docs/agents/` — does this skill's prior output already exist?

1→# CONTEXT.md Format

## Structure

```md
# {Context Name}

{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}

10→## Language

**Order**:
{A one or two sentence description of the term}
_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction

**Invoice**:
A request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.
_Avoid_: Bill, payment request

20→**Customer**:
A person or organization that places orders.
_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account
```

## Rules

- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.
- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.
- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.
30→- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.

## Single vs multi-context repos

**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.

**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:

```md
# Context Map
40→
## Contexts

- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md) — receives and tracks customer orders
- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md) — generates invoices and processes payments
- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md) — manages warehouse picking and shipping

## Relationships

- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking
50→- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices
- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`
```

The skill infers which structure applies:

- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts
- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context
- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved

60→When multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.

1→---
name: to-spec
description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

This skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user — just synthesize what you already know.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.
10→
## Process

1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.

2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.

Check with the user that these seams match their expectations.

3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.
20→
<spec-template>

## Problem Statement

The problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.

## Solution

The solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.
30→
## User Stories

A LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:

1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>

<user-story-example>
1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending
</user-story-example>
40→
This list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.

## Implementation Decisions

A list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:

- The modules that will be built/modified
- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified
- Technical clarifications from the developer
50→- Architectural decisions
- Schema changes
- API contracts
- Specific interactions

Do NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.

Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

## Testing Decisions
60→
A list of testing decisions that were made. Include:

110→## Implementation Decisions

- One repo plus one runtime. Doraval authors the grill skill under `skills/` and grows the `dora harness` group. Hermes is configured, not forked. The kit does not own this work.
- The user-facing object is a **routine**. Hermes still stores a cron **job**. The teammate hears “routine.”
- Routine path: `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. Slug comes from the grill and may be renamed. Commands take the slug.
- Routine contents (contract, not file names): unattended prompt, skill directories to run, skill directories to refer to, MCP URL, interval, max tick. The shape is extensible. Secrets do not live in a file that an optional git remote would publish.
- Default schedule: every 1 hour. Default max tick: 10 minutes (Hermes 600s). Both are per-routine and may be changed later by the grill or by `dora harness`.
- `dora harness` verbs: `new`, `boot`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, `open`. `resume` is required because pause must reverse. `open` opens the routine folder.
- Bare `boot` lists routines and lets the teammate pick one or start create (same path as `new`). `boot <slug>` boots that routine.
- Boot sequence: if Hermes is missing, print official install steps and stop. If Hermes is present, ensure the gateway is running as a machine service, write one cron job from the routine (toolset includes `mcp-<server>`), then exit. Dora does not own a timer.
120→- Pause calls `hermes cron pause` for that job. Job state becomes `paused`. Gateway stays up. A running pass may finish. Resume calls `hermes cron resume`.
- Laptop close is host sleep. Official Hermes: cron does not run while the host sleeps. Sleep is not pause.
- Scalekit is a normal HTTP MCP server in Hermes (`url` plus `auth: oauth`). It is not the Nous Tool Gateway. The teammate pastes the MCP URL. Dora does not mint Virtual MCP session tokens with API keys.
- First connect is Hermes OAuth / magic link. Scalekit stores provider tokens. Hermes stores MCP login under `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/`. Later ticks reuse those files. Refresh is automatic while the refresh token is valid.
- Refresh fail or missing cache: stop and tell the human to run `hermes mcp login <server>`. A dead connected account: stop and tell the human to open the provider link again. Cron has no TTY. Do not pretend a browser flow will work at night.
- Grill skill: we author it in doraval under `skills/`. Ship with `dora review --quick` on that skill directory. Do not draft it in the kit. Do not update kit `ask-saif`.
- Grill shape: mirror `grill-with-docs`. Pragmatic gate before save: skills to run, skills to refer to, Scalekit Agent Gateway URL. Then `writing-for-agents` writes the unattended prompt. Then one test pass (print the command, or an interactive flow). Then write the routine folder.
- Later, steal Warp skill-doctor checks that fit. Those checks are not a v1 gate.
- Dora may later copy a routine to skillkit, or point at a repo of routines. Not required for v1.
- Optional `dora review` on attached skill directories. Skip is fine.
130→- User brings LLM credits. This spec does not provision a model key.
- Do not write loop product terms into kit `CONTEXT.md`. Kit glossary stays the language of the kit.
- First wording is for an internal teammate. Do not pick a first sample use case.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate can see or what Dora writes. It does not check Hermes internals. It does not start a live gateway in CI. It does not run a real Scalekit OAuth dance.

### Seams

140→1. **Primary seam: `dora harness` CLI (doraval).** Assert help text, missing-Hermes install steps, routine folder write, and the Hermes commands Dora would run for boot, pause, resume, and list. Prefer doraval’s existing command-tree / CLI tests.
2. **Secondary seam: grill skill in doraval `skills/`.** Assert `dora review <skill-dir> --quick` exits 0. Also assert the skill names the pragmatic gate and the one-pass-then-save order. Do not automate the interview.
3. **Shared artifact: routine folder contract.** The folder is the seam between Dora and Hermes. Assert slug, prompt, skill dirs, MCP URL, interval, and max tick are present. Do not assert Hermes job JSON schema beyond what Dora is specified to write.

### Modules under test

- Doraval `harness` group (behavior at the CLI).
- Grill skill (review plus the documented gate and order).
- Routine folder writer (contract above).

150→### Prior art

- Doraval: `dora review --quick` on the grill skill. Closed command tree plus CLI tests for each verb. New group follows that pattern.
- No Hermes test double that reimplements cron.

## Out of Scope

- A new CLI beside Dora.
- Hermes Tool Gateway as the Slack (or any connector) path.
- Minting Scalekit session tokens with API keys (Virtual MCP mint path).
160→- Claude, Grok, or OpenCode as the runtime in this spec.
- The whole product as “a kit skill.” The grill skill lives in doraval. The runner is still Dora plus Hermes.
- Picking a first sample use case (Discord, GitHub, or OOO). The spec stays generic.
- Wording and docs for “anyone with the stack.” First reader is an internal teammate.
- Company setup on more than one machine.
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Dora sitting on the magic link / OAuth path.
- Push, webhooks, or a Hermes Slack bot. The interval is the trigger.
- Making skillkit the default skill directory.
- Writing loop terms into kit `CONTEXT.md`. Doraval `CONTEXT.md` may gain routine / harness / loop terms when the group ships.
170→- Shipping the grill skill in this spec session. Spec first. Tickets next.

## Further Notes

Map: [Local use cases](map.md).

Research:

- Loop runners survey: `docs/research/2026-08-28-always-on-loop-runners.md`
- Hermes cron and MCP OAuth: `docs/research/2026-08-29-hermes-cron-mcp-oauth.md`

218→## Harness (shipped)

220→`dora harness` is the front desk. The Runtime ticks the Loop. Today the Runtime is Hermes. 2026-08-31.

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Routine** | Saved folder at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. The only product object. _Avoid_: pack. |
| **Loop** | The same unattended prompt on an interval. The Runtime's timer. Default 1 hour. |
| **Tick** | One unattended run of a Loop. The Runtime starts it on the interval. Not the one-pass test. _Avoid_: night tick as a second object. |
| **Runtime** | The background agent that ticks a Loop. Today that agent is Hermes. Dora prints that Runtime's watch commands. _Avoid_: calling Hermes the product; a second Runtime in this pass. |
| **Max tick** | One-pass wall clock via the Runtime. Default 10 minutes. Night idle cap is the Runtime's idle timeout (Hermes: `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`, default 600s). |
| **Harness** | Verbs: `new`, `boot`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, `open`. |
230→| **Skill script** | A helper file inside a Skill folder. The Skill names the path. The routine has no top-level scripts directory. _Avoid_: routine script; Hermes `--script`. |
| **Fixed step** | A deterministic routine step stored in a Skill. `prompt.md` names that Skill. It does not repeat the step. _Avoid_: programmatize as a noun; Judgment (that word is a Dora Finding). |
| **Pocket** | Size check on a Routine idea. One job, one machine, one user. The night prompt must be specific. |
| **Pocket agent** | Reader name for that small loop. The saved folder is still a Routine. _Avoid_: a second folder type. |
| **Tick handoff** | File `handoff.md` in the routine folder. Next Tick reads it. This Tick overwrites it. Missing file means first Tick. Prefer the destination as the store. _Avoid_: Hermes notepad-with-slug; MEMORY.md as a cursor. |

_Avoid_: Dora on the OAuth / magic-link path; Slack, Discord, or Webflow in the harness; writing loop terms into kit CONTEXT.md.

## Naming debt (intentional)

# Harness management

Date: 2026-09-04
Status: ready-for-agent
Parent: [Local use-case runner](../local-use-cases/spec.md) · #79–#83 (shipped)

Grill closed 2026-09-04. Process: Matt Pocock `grilling` → `to-spec` → `to-tickets` → `implement`.

## Problem Statement

A Routine already exists. The teammate and the coding agent cannot manage it from Dora.

`list` shows only a slug and a coarse state. There is no card for one Routine. There is no way to see that job’s ticks. Pause and resume pass a slug to a Runtime that wants a job id, so they miss the live job. A second `boot` creates a second job. There is no delete. There is no push after the folder changes.

`ask-dora` still names only `boot`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, and `open`. An agent that must act has no copy-paste verb for apply, show, logs, or remove.

## Solution

Dora stays the front desk. The folder stays the source of truth. The teammate and the agent type a **slug**. Dora maps the Runtime job id.

`apply` pushes the folder onto the Runtime job. First time it creates the job and stores the id. Later it edits that id. `boot` is the same command. Help and `ask-dora` lead with `apply`.

`list` is a table. `show` is the card for one Routine. `list <slug>` is `show`. `logs` asks with slugs, then prints that job’s ticks. `rm` stops that job, then deletes the folder.

Agents act through the same verbs. They pass a slug. They use `--yes` / `--dry-run` on writes and `--json` on reads. They do not type a hex id. They do not need a TTY picker.

## User Stories

1. As a teammate, I want `dora harness list` to show slug, state, interval, and last run, so that I can scan every Routine.
2. As a teammate, I want `dora harness show <slug>` to print one card, so that I do not open the folder to learn state.
3. As a teammate, I want that card to show slug, state, interval, max tick, MCP yes or none, last run, and folder path, so that I see the contract.
4. As a teammate, I do not want the card to print the full prompt or secrets, so that `open` stays the way to read files.
5. As a teammate, I want the hex job id only in `--json`, so that the default card stays human.
6. As a teammate, I want `dora harness list <slug>` to be the same as `show`, so that a wrong guess still works.
7. As a teammate, I want bare `dora harness` to stay the list, so that the front desk does not change.
8. As a teammate, I want `dora harness apply <slug>` to push the folder onto the Runtime job, so that an edited prompt or interval actually runs.
9. As a teammate, I want a first `apply` to create the Runtime job and remember its id, so that later verbs hit the same job.
10. As a teammate, I want a later `apply` to edit that job, so that I do not get a second job.
11. As a teammate, I want `dora harness boot` to do the same as `apply`, so that old commands and old skill lines still work.
12. As a teammate, I want help and `ask-dora` to lead with `apply`, so that new readers learn one word.
13. As a teammate, I do not want `dora harness set`, so that there is one way to change the folder: edit the files.
14. As a teammate, I want to change `prompt.md` or `routine.yml` with `open` or an editor, then `apply`, so that the folder stays the editor.
15. As a coding agent, I want to write those files and then run `dora harness apply <slug> --yes`, so that I can finish without a TTY.
16. As a teammate, I want `apply` to start the Runtime gateway if it is down, so that a first attach still works.
17. As a teammate, I want missing Hermes on `apply` to print official install steps and stop, so that Dora does not fake a push.
18. As a teammate, I want a dead stored id to make `apply` create a new job and write the new id, so that I can attach again.
19. As a teammate, I want `pause`, `resume`, and `logs` to say the job is gone when the id is dead, so that I know to `apply`.
20. As a teammate, I want `rm` to delete the folder even when the job is already gone, so that a leftover folder is not stuck.
21. As a teammate, I want `rm` to stop if the job is still there and remove fails, so that I do not orphan a running job.
22. As a teammate with old Routines that have no stored id, I want the first verb that needs the id to match Runtime name to slug and write the id, so that I do not get a second job.
23. As a teammate, I want pause and resume to use that stored id, so that they hit the live job.
24. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs` to list slugs and let me pick, so that I never type a hex id.
25. As a teammate, I want that pick to run the Runtime’s per-job run history for that id, so that I see ticks for that Routine only.
26. As a teammate, I do not want `logs` to dump the global Runtime agent log, so that I am not reading every job at once.
27. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs <slug>` to skip the picker, so that I can type the slug I already know.
28. As a teammate, I want `dora harness rm <slug>` to stop that job and then delete the folder, so that delete is one verb.
29. As a teammate, I want `rm` to require `--yes` (or a TTY confirm), so that a slip does not wipe a Routine.
30. As a teammate, I want bare `pause`, `resume`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` to pick from slugs when I am on a TTY, so that I do not remember names.
31. As a teammate, I want `rm` after a pick to still need `--yes`, so that a pick is not a delete.
32. As a coding agent, I want no picker when there is no TTY, so that I do not hang.
33. As a coding agent, I want that no-TTY path to print slugs, exit `2`, and print the next command with a slug, so that I can retry.
34. As a coding agent, I want every new or changed verb in `dora --help --json` with a copy-paste example, so that I have a live map.
35. As a coding agent, I want writes (`apply`, `boot`, `rm`) to refuse me unless I pass `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that I do not write by accident.
36. As a coding agent, I want reads (`list`, `show`, `logs`, `pause`, `resume`) to accept `--json`, so that I get one object or one list on stdout.
37. As a coding agent, I want to type only a slug, so that I never handle a Runtime job id.
38. As a coding agent, I want a next command printed after each verb, so that I know the next act.
39. As a coding agent, I want exit `0` on success, `1` on a failed act, and `2` when I could not run (no slug, no Hermes when required, omitted `--yes` on a write), so that I can branch.
40. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want that skill to name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, so that I do not load the grill.
41. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want `boot` still accepted as the apply alias, so that old prompts work.
42. As a teammate, I want `review-with-dora` and `grilling-for-routine` to name the same verbs, so that the four shipped skills do not lie.
43. As a first reader, I want website `/commands/harness`, Connect/pocket-agent pages if they name verbs, and the README catalog to match the binary, so that docs lockstep holds.
44. As a teammate, I want interval on apply to become the Runtime schedule, so that a yaml change is real.
45. As a teammate, I want max tick to stay as it is today (one-pass budget / Runtime idle), so that we do not invent a new timeout flag.
46. As a teammate, I want `open` unchanged, so that I can still edit files by hand.
47. As a teammate, I want `new` unchanged, so that create stays the grill path.
48. As a teammate, I want laptop close to stay sleep, not pause, so that v1 meaning does not change.
49. As a teammate, I want Dora to stay off the OAuth / magic-link path, so that I still run Runtime login in a real terminal.
50. As a doraval maintainer, I want this spec in its own file, so that the shipped v1 spec stays history.
51. As a doraval maintainer, I want rename parked, so that this pass stays small.
52. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `apply` to print the Runtime commands and write nothing, so that I can preview.
53. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `rm` to print the plan and delete nothing, so that I can preview.
54. As a teammate, I want list state `none` when there is no Runtime job, so that an unbooted folder is visible.
55. As a teammate, I want list state running or paused from the Runtime when the id is known, so that the table matches the timer.
56. As a teammate, I want last run taken from the Runtime list when present, so that Dora does not invent a second history store.

## Implementation Decisions

- This is an addendum pass on the shipped harness. Hermes stays the only Runtime. Dora does not own a timer.
- The teammate-facing key is the slug. The Runtime-facing key is the job id (12-char hex on each create). Dora stores that id on the Routine after a successful create or a successful name backfill.
- Folder wins when the folder and the job disagree. `apply` is the push. There is no pull from the Runtime into the folder.
- `apply` and `boot` are one implementation. Canonical name in help, `dora --help --json`, and `ask-dora` is `apply`. `boot` remains a working alias.
- First `apply` (no stored id, and no name match): ensure the Runtime gateway is up, create one job from the folder (name = slug, schedule from interval, prompt from the folder, skills to run attached), parse the new id, store it, exit.
- Later `apply` (stored id still on the Runtime): edit that job’s schedule, prompt, and skills from the folder. Do not create.
- Stored id missing on the Runtime: create, store the new id (same as first apply).
- No stored id, but a Runtime job name equals the slug: write that id, then edit. Do not create a second job.
- Pause and resume use the stored id. They do not pass the slug to the Runtime.
- `logs` with a slug (or after a pick) runs the Runtime per-job run history for that id. It does not wrap the global agent log.
- `rm` removes that id on the Runtime if the job exists, then deletes the Routine folder. If remove fails and the job still exists, stop and keep the folder. If the job is already gone, delete the folder.
- `rm` and `apply` are writes. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run`.
- Bare verbs on a TTY pick from slugs. `rm` after a pick still needs `--yes`. No TTY: no picker; print slugs; exit `2`; print the next command with a slug.
- `list` columns: slug, state, interval, last run. State is running, paused, or none.
- `show` card: slug, state, interval, max tick, MCP yes or none, last run, folder path. Hex id only in `--json`. No full prompt. No secrets. No `.env`.
- `list <slug>` is `show`.
- No `set`. No `rename` in this pass.
- Interval maps to the Runtime schedule flag. Max tick is unchanged from v1 (one-pass budget / Runtime idle env).
- Agent contract is required: every new or changed verb on `dora --help --json` with an example; slug only; `--json` on reads; `--yes` / `--dry-run` on writes; next command after each verb; exits `0` / `1` / `2` as in the stories.
- Docs lockstep in the same change as the verbs: README command catalog, website harness command page, `ask-dora`, `review-with-dora`, `grilling-for-routine` (and `writing-for-routine` only if it names harness verbs).
- Do not bump the version unless the user asks for a release.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate or an agent can see, or what Dora writes to the Routine folder. It does not start a live Runtime gateway in CI. It does not run a real OAuth dance.

### Seams

1. **Primary seam: `dora harness` CLI.** Assert help text, `dora --help --json` examples, missing-Hermes install steps, `--yes` / `--dry-run` write gate, `--json` shapes, exit codes, picker vs no-TTY, and the Runtime argument lists Dora would run for apply (create vs edit), pause, resume, logs, and rm. Prefer the existing harness CLI tests and a fake Runtime binary on `PATH`.
2. **Shared artifact: Routine folder.** Assert the stored job id is written on create and on name backfill. Assert `rm` deletes the folder only when the spec allows. Do not assert Runtime job JSON schema beyond what Dora is specified to write.
3. **Shipped skills.** Assert `ask-dora` and the review/grill skills name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, and still accept `boot`. Assert `dora review --quick` on those skill directories still exits 0.

Do not add a new seam. Do not parse live Hermes in CI.

### Modules under test

- Harness group (CLI behavior).
- Routine folder read/write (id field, rm).
- Runtime command builder (create vs edit vs pause vs resume vs remove vs runs).
- Shipped skills (named verbs).

### Prior art

- Existing harness CLI tests with a fake `hermes` on `PATH`.
- `dora --help --json` / capabilities tests for new examples.
- Docs lockstep tests that already pin harness wording.

## Out of Scope

- Rename of a slug or a Runtime job name.
- `dora harness set` or any second edit API.
- A Dora verb that wraps the global Runtime agent log.
- A repo of Routines, a git remote on the folder, a copy into skillkit.
- Config UI, Config sync, identity probe.
- A second Runtime (Claude, Grok, OpenCode).
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Dora sitting on the OAuth / magic-link path.
- Changing max tick mapping to a new Runtime flag.
- Rewriting the v1 spec.
- A version bump unless the user asks.

## Further Notes

Parent v1: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

Live Runtime (fact, 2026-09-04): `cron edit` and `cron remove` exist. `pause`, `resume`, `edit`, `remove`, and `runs` take a job id. `cron list` prints the hex id and `[active]` on one line and `Name:` on the next. Last run is on that list. v1 list parse and v1 pause-by-slug do not match that output. This pass must.

Research already in tree: agent-browser CLI notes (`docs/research-notes/46-agent-browser-cli-ux.md`, `50-cli-command-structure.md`); Hermes tick-state (`docs/research-notes/55-hermes-tick-state.md`).

Next skill: `/to-tickets`. Then `/implement` per ticket in a fresh session.

14. As a teammate, I want to change `prompt.md` or `routine.yml` with `open` or an editor, then `apply`, so that the folder stays the editor.
15. As a coding agent, I want to write those files and then run `dora harness apply <slug> --yes`, so that I can finish without a TTY.
16. As a teammate, I want `apply` to start the Runtime gateway if it is down, so that a first attach still works.
17. As a teammate, I want missing Hermes on `apply` to print official install steps and stop, so that Dora does not fake a push.
18. As a teammate, I want a dead stored id to make `apply` create a new job and write the new id, so that I can attach again.
19. As a teammate, I want `pause`, `resume`, and `logs` to say the job is gone when the id is dead, so that I know to `apply`.
20. As a teammate, I want `rm` to delete the folder even when the job is already gone, so that a leftover folder is not stuck.
21. As a teammate, I want `rm` to stop if the job is still there and remove fails, so that I do not orphan a running job.
22. As a teammate with old Routines that have no stored id, I want the first verb that needs the id to match Runtime name to slug and write the id, so that I do not get a second job.
23. As a teammate, I want pause and resume to use that stored id, so that they hit the live job.
24. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs` to list slugs and let me pick, so that I never type a hex id.
25. As a teammate, I want that pick to run the Runtime’s per-job run history for that id, so that I see ticks for that Routine only.
26. As a teammate, I do not want `logs` to dump the global Runtime agent log, so that I am not reading every job at once.
27. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs <slug>` to skip the picker, so that I can type the slug I already know.
28. As a teammate, I want `dora harness rm <slug>` to stop that job and then delete the folder, so that delete is one verb.
29. As a teammate, I want `rm` to require `--yes` (or a TTY confirm), so that a slip does not wipe a Routine.
30. As a teammate, I want bare `pause`, `resume`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` to pick from slugs when I am on a TTY, so that I do not remember names.
31. As a teammate, I want `rm` after a pick to still need `--yes`, so that a pick is not a delete.
32. As a coding agent, I want no picker when there is no TTY, so that I do not hang.
33. As a coding agent, I want that no-TTY path to print slugs, exit `2`, and print the next command with a slug, so that I can retry.
34. As a coding agent, I want every new or changed verb in `dora --help --json` with a copy-paste example, so that I have a live map.
35. As a coding agent, I want writes (`apply`, `boot`, `rm`) to refuse me unless I pass `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that I do not write by accident.
36. As a coding agent, I want reads (`list`, `show`, `logs`, `pause`, `resume`) to accept `--json`, so that I get one object or one list on stdout.
37. As a coding agent, I want to type only a slug, so that I never handle a Runtime job id.
38. As a coding agent, I want a next command printed after each verb, so that I know the next act.
39. As a coding agent, I want exit `0` on success, `1` on a failed act, and `2` when I could not run (no slug, no Hermes when required, omitted `--yes` on a write), so that I can branch.
40. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want that skill to name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, so that I do not load the grill.
41. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want `boot` still accepted as the apply alias, so that old prompts work.
42. As a teammate, I want `review-with-dora` and `grilling-for-routine` to name the same verbs, so that the four shipped skills do not lie.
43. As a first reader, I want website `/commands/harness`, Connect/pocket-agent pages if they name verbs, and the README catalog to match the binary, so that docs lockstep holds.
44. As a teammate, I want interval on apply to become the Runtime schedule, so that a yaml change is real.
45. As a teammate, I want max tick to stay as it is today (one-pass budget / Runtime idle), so that we do not invent a new timeout flag.
46. As a teammate, I want `open` unchanged, so that I can still edit files by hand.
47. As a teammate, I want `new` unchanged, so that create stays the grill path.
48. As a teammate, I want laptop close to stay sleep, not pause, so that v1 meaning does not change.
49. As a teammate, I want Dora to stay off the OAuth / magic-link path, so that I still run Runtime login in a real terminal.
50. As a doraval maintainer, I want this spec in its own file, so that the shipped v1 spec stays history.
51. As a doraval maintainer, I want rename parked, so that this pass stays small.
52. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `apply` to print the Runtime commands and write nothing, so that I can preview.
53. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `rm` to print the plan and delete nothing, so that I can preview.
54. As a teammate, I want list state `none` when there is no Runtime job, so that an unbooted folder is visible.
55. As a teammate, I want list state running or paused from the Runtime when the id is known, so that the table matches the timer.
56. As a teammate, I want last run taken from the Runtime list when present, so that Dora does not invent a second history store.

## Implementation Decisions

- This is an addendum pass on the shipped harness. Hermes stays the only Runtime. Dora does not own a timer.
- The teammate-facing key is the slug. The Runtime-facing key is the job id (12-char hex on each create). Dora stores that id on the Routine after a successful create or a successful name backfill.
- Folder wins when the folder and the job disagree. `apply` is the push. There is no pull from the Runtime into the folder.
- `apply` and `boot` are one implementation. Canonical name in help, `dora --help --json`, and `ask-dora` is `apply`. `boot` remains a working alias.
- First `apply` (no stored id, and no name match): ensure the Runtime gateway is up, create one job from the folder (name = slug, schedule from interval, prompt from the folder, skills to run attached), parse the new id, store it, exit.
- Later `apply` (stored id still on the Runtime): edit that job’s schedule, prompt, and skills from the folder. Do not create.
- Stored id missing on the Runtime: create, store the new id (same as first apply).
- No stored id, but a Runtime job name equals the slug: write that id, then edit. Do not create a second job.
- Pause and resume use the stored id. They do not pass the slug to the Runtime.
- `logs` with a slug (or after a pick) runs the Runtime per-job run history for that id. It does not wrap the global agent log.
- `rm` removes that id on the Runtime if the job exists, then deletes the Routine folder. If remove fails and the job still exists, stop and keep the folder. If the job is already gone, delete the folder.
- `rm` and `apply` are writes. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run`.
- Bare verbs on a TTY pick from slugs. `rm` after a pick still needs `--yes`. No TTY: no picker; print slugs; exit `2`; print the next command with a slug.
- `list` columns: slug, state, interval, last run. State is running, paused, or none.
- `show` card: slug, state, interval, max tick, MCP yes or none, last run, folder path. Hex id only in `--json`. No full prompt. No secrets. No `.env`.
- `list <slug>` is `show`.
- No `set`. No `rename` in this pass.
- Interval maps to the Runtime schedule flag. Max tick is unchanged from v1 (one-pass budget / Runtime idle env).
- Agent contract is required: every new or changed verb on `dora --help --json` with an example; slug only; `--json` on reads; `--yes` / `--dry-run` on writes; next command after each verb; exits `0` / `1` / `2` as in the stories.
- Docs lockstep in the same change as the verbs: README command catalog, website harness command page, `ask-dora`, `review-with-dora`, `grilling-for-routine` (and `writing-for-routine` only if it names harness verbs).
- Do not bump the version unless the user asks for a release.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate or an agent can see, or what Dora writes to the Routine folder. It does not start a live Runtime gateway in CI. It does not run a real OAuth dance.

### Seams

1. **Primary seam: `dora harness` CLI.** Assert help text, `dora --help --json` examples, missing-Hermes install steps, `--yes` / `--dry-run` write gate, `--json` shapes, exit codes, picker vs no-TTY, and the Runtime argument lists Dora would run for apply (create vs edit), pause, resume, logs, and rm. Prefer the existing harness CLI tests and a fake Runtime binary on `PATH`.
2. **Shared artifact: Routine folder.** Assert the stored job id is written on create and on name backfill. Assert `rm` deletes the folder only when the spec allows. Do not assert Runtime job JSON schema beyond what Dora is specified to write.
3. **Shipped skills.** Assert `ask-dora` and the review/grill skills name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, and still accept `boot`. Assert `dora review --quick` on those skill directories still exits 0.

Do not add a new seam. Do not parse live Hermes in CI.

### Modules under test

- Harness group (CLI behavior).
- Routine folder read/write (id field, rm).
- Runtime command builder (create vs edit vs pause vs resume vs remove vs runs).
- Shipped skills (named verbs).

### Prior art

- Existing harness CLI tests with a fake `hermes` on `PATH`.
- `dora --help --json` / capabilities tests for new examples.
- Docs lockstep tests that already pin harness wording.

## Out of Scope

- Rename of a slug or a Runtime job name.
- `dora harness set` or any second edit API.
- A Dora verb that wraps the global Runtime agent log.
- A repo of Routines, a git remote on the folder, a copy into skillkit.
- Config UI, Config sync, identity probe.
- A second Runtime (Claude, Grok, OpenCode).
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Dora sitting on the OAuth / magic-link path.
- Changing max tick mapping to a new Runtime flag.
- Rewriting the v1 spec.
- A version bump unless the user asks.

## Further Notes

Parent v1: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

Live Runtime (fact, 2026-09-04): `cron edit` and `cron remove` exist. `pause`, `resume`, `edit`, `remove`, and `runs` take a job id. `cron list` prints the hex id and `[active]` on one line and `Name:` on the next. Last run is on that list. v1 list parse and v1 pause-by-slug do not match that output. This pass must.

Research already in tree: agent-browser CLI notes (`docs/research-notes/46-agent-browser-cli-ux.md`, `50-cli-command-structure.md`); Hermes tick-state (`docs/research-notes/55-hermes-tick-state.md`).

Next skill: `/to-tickets`. Then `/implement` per ticket in a fresh session.

| **Tick** | One unattended run of a Loop. The Runtime starts it on the interval. Not the one-pass test. _Avoid_: night tick as a second object. |
| **Runtime** | The background agent that ticks a Loop. Today that agent is Hermes. Dora prints that Runtime's watch commands. _Avoid_: calling Hermes the product; a second Runtime in this pass. |

details.context_after:
| **Skill script** | A helper file inside a Skill folder. The Skill names the path. The routine has no top-level scripts directory. _Avoid_: routine script; Hermes `--script`. |
| **Fixed step** | A deterministic routine step stored in a Skill. `prompt.md` names that Skill. It does not repeat the step. _Avoid_: programmatize as a noun; Judgment (that word is a Dora Finding). |
| **Pocket** | Size check on a Routine idea. One job, one machine, one user. The night prompt must be specific. |

Each ticket is a vertical slice. Agent rules (`--json`, `--yes`, slug only, `dora --help --json`) live **inside** that ticket’s verbs. They are not a separate ticket.

**1. See: job id, list, and show**  
**Blocked by:** none

**Blocked by:** 1

last_assistant_message:
Agents are a first-class user of these verbs. That is locked in the spec. It is not a footnote.

**What an agent does**

- Types a **slug**. Never a Hermes hex id. Dora maps the id.
- Writes with `--yes` or `--dry-run` (`apply`, `boot`, `rm`).
- Reads with `--json` (`list`, `show`, `logs`, `pause`, `resume`).
- Uses `dora --help --json` as the live map. Every new verb has a copy-paste example there.
- Gets a **next command** after each run.
- Branches on exit `0` / `1` / `2`.

**What an agent does not do**

- Sit in a TTY picker. No TTY → print slugs, exit `2`, print the command with a slug.
- Call `set`. It writes the files, then `dora harness apply <slug> --yes`.
- Load the grill for an existing Routine. `ask-dora` names `apply`, `show`, `logs`, `rm`. `boot` still works as the alias.

**How that hits the tickets**

There is no “make it agent-friendly” ticket. Each ticket ships that contract for **its** verbs. Ticket 5 then teaches `ask-dora` and the docs the same names.

A human picker is extra. The main path is a command an agent can type.
